# Button

Primary, secondary, tertiary, and destructive actions in three sizes, with loading and icon-only modes.

```tsx
import { Button } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `button` |
| Family | buttons |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | `state-layer`, `spinner` |

## Behavior

Activation guarding and disabled/busy semantics, independent of React and of any styling.

Headless contract: `getButtonProps` in `packages/primitives/src/button.ts` — importable from `@rata/primitives` without the React wrapper or any CSS.

- **`aria-disabled` instead of the native `disabled` attribute** — A natively disabled button leaves the tab order and stops being announced, so users navigating by keyboard or screen reader cannot discover that the action exists. Activation is blocked in the click guard instead.
- **`loading` implies inert** — One flag covers both halves of what callers actually want — show progress, and refuse a second click — so the two cannot be set inconsistently.

## Props

Extends `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "disabled">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant?` | `ButtonVariant` | `"primary"` | Which action tier this button occupies, and therefore how loud it is. |
| `size?` | `ButtonSize` | `"md"` | Control height and inline padding, from the `size.control.*` scale. Text size does not change with it. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks activation while keeping the button focusable and announced. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | — | Shows a spinner and refuses activation while an operation is in flight. |
| `iconOnly?` | `boolean` | — | Square button carrying an icon and no visible text. |

### `variant`

```ts
variant?: ButtonVariant = "primary"
```

Which action tier this button occupies, and therefore how loud it is.

**Use when**

- `primary` for the single highest-priority action in a view — one per view.
- `secondary` for a supporting action shown beside a primary one.
- `tertiary` for low-emphasis actions in dense areas, like a row action.
- `destructive` for an action that deletes or revokes something.

**Don't use for**

- Two `primary` buttons in one view — the tier is a claim about priority, and two claims cancel out.
- `destructive` for merely irreversible actions like Submit; it means data is lost.

**Accessibility** Variant is visual only. A destructive action still needs its own confirmation step — colour is not a warning.

### `size`

```ts
size?: ButtonSize = "md"
```

Control height and inline padding, from the `size.control.*` scale. Text size does not change with it.

**Use when**

- `md` everywhere by default.
- `sm` inside dense rows, toolbars, and table cells.
- `lg` for a single prominent call to action on a marketing or empty-state surface.

**Don't use for**

- Shrinking to `sm` to fit a cramped layout — fix the layout budget instead.
- Expecting the label to grow with it. All three sizes set the same text size, so `size` buys a bigger target for the same action rather than a louder one — and an icon inside, being sized from that text, does not change either.
- Setting height or padding yourself; the size prop is the only supported way to change either.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks activation while keeping the button focusable and announced.

**Use when**

- An action that is unavailable for a reason the surrounding UI already explains.

**Don't use for**

- Hiding why an action is unavailable — pair it with visible helper text or a tooltip.
- Form validation gating, where an inline error explains more than a dead button does.

**Conflicts with** `loading`

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-disabled`, never the native `disabled` attribute: the control stays in the tab order and discoverable by screen readers, and activation is blocked in the primitive's click guard.

### `loading`

```ts
loading?: boolean
```

Shows a spinner and refuses activation while an operation is in flight.

Source doc: Shows a spinner and blocks activation while preserving focus.

**Use when**

- Async work started by this button, so the same control reports its own progress.

**Don't use for**

- Page-level or unrelated loading — that belongs to the region that is actually loading.
- Swapping the label to 'Loading…' as well; the spinner and `aria-busy` already say it, and a changing label loses the action's name.

**Conflicts with** `disabled`

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-busy` alongside `aria-disabled`, so assistive technology hears both that the control is working and that it will not respond yet.

### `iconOnly`

```ts
iconOnly?: boolean
```

Square button carrying an icon and no visible text.

Source doc: Square icon-only button; pass the icon as children and set aria-label.

**Use when**

- Dense toolbars and row actions where the icon is unambiguous and repeated.
- Icon-only buttons in this system: there is no separate `IconButton` component, and one would be a second way to do what this prop already does.

**Don't use for**

- Any action whose icon is not already conventional — an unlabelled novel icon is unreadable.
- Passing text children as well; the square sizing assumes a single glyph.

**Accessibility** You MUST pass `aria-label`. Nothing in the component supplies an accessible name when there is no visible text.

## Use cases

### Primary action with async work

The most common pairing: one primary button that owns its own progress.

```tsx
<Button loading={saving} onClick={save}>Save changes</Button>
```

`loading` blocks repeat activation on its own — don't also guard with `disabled`.

### Destructive action in a confirmation

Deleting something, with the safe action given equal visual weight beside it.

```tsx
<Button variant="destructive" onClick={remove}>Delete project</Button>
```

### Icon-only row action

A dense table row where a labelled button would not fit.

```tsx
<Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Remove row">×</Button>
```

Without `aria-label` this button has no accessible name at all.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Button>Publish</Button>
```

## Token recipe

### primary

The single highest-priority action in a view.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.accent-role.bg` |
| color | `theme.fg.on-accent` |
| height | `size.control.md — and size.control.sm / .lg at the other sizes; this is the only thing `size` changes` |
| padding-inline | `space.control.padding-inline.md` |
| gap | `space.gap.xs` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| font-size | `type.control.size.md — constant across all three sizes, so `size` changes the box and not the label` |
| font-weight | `type.control.weight` |
| line-height | `type.control.line-height.md — constant, as with font-size` |
| transition-duration | `motion.interactive.duration` |
| transition-timing-function | `motion.interactive.easing` |
| outline (focus-visible) | `focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset` |
| hover/press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class — do not swap the background` |

### secondary

A supporting action shown next to a primary one. Its label is accent-toned rather than neutral, so the outlined button still reads as an action and not as a disabled box — the border alone carries very little at this fill.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.secondary-role.bg` |
| color | `theme.accent-role.fg` |
| border-color | `theme.secondary-role.border` |
| height | `size.control.md — and size.control.sm / .lg at the other sizes; this is the only thing `size` changes` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| hover/press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class` |

### destructive

An action that deletes or revokes something.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.danger-role.bg` |
| color | `theme.fg.on-accent` |
| height | `size.control.md — and size.control.sm / .lg at the other sizes; this is the only thing `size` changes` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| hover/press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class` |
